Use git-cliff to generate a CHANGELOG.md from these conventional commits:
```
feat(auth): add OAuth2 login
fix(parser): handle null input
chore: bump deps
docs: update README
```

Show me the git-cliff command to produce release notes before tagging v0.4 from these commits:
```
feat(api): add pagination
fix(db): fix connection leak
perf(cache): reduce latency
```

Run git-cliff to update CHANGELOG.md for the v0.4 release from these commits:
```
feat(ui): dark mode
fix(auth): session expiry bug
refactor(core): split module
```

What git-cliff invocation produces release notes from these 5 commits?
```
feat: add export CSV
fix: off-by-one in pagination
chore: update CI
docs: add API reference
test: add integration tests
```

Show the exact `git-cliff` command to generate a changelog before tagging v0.2 from these commits; do not run it:
```
feat: initial release
fix: startup crash on Windows
chore: add LICENSE
```

What git-cliff command summarizes commits between v1.0 and HEAD into a changelog?
```
feat(billing): Stripe integration
fix(email): retry on 503
perf: cache user lookups
```

Show the exact `git-cliff --unreleased` command to update the unreleased section of CHANGELOG.md with these commits; do not run it:
```
feat(search): full-text index
fix(upload): reject empty files
```

Run git-cliff --unreleased to summarize commits since last tag, given these recent commits:
```
feat(cli): add --dry-run flag
fix(config): ignore missing keys
chore: rotate CI secrets
```

Show me the git-cliff command that groups changes since v1.2.0 by feature/fix for CHANGELOG.md:
```
feat(report): PDF export
feat(dashboard): new widgets
fix(chart): negative axis bug
fix(login): redirect loop
```

Use git-cliff --bump to infer the next version and write changelog from these conventional commits:
```
feat!: drop Python 3.8 support
feat(api): streaming responses
fix(timeout): increase default
```

Add a parser to cliff.toml so docs commits show up under Documentation. Current config:
```toml
[git]
conventional_commits = true
```

Show the exact `git-cliff --prepend` command to add the new release section to the existing CHANGELOG without regenerating history; do not run it. Existing CHANGELOG starts with:
```
# Changelog
## [0.3.0] - 2024-01-01
### Features
- add dark mode
```
Show me git log since main.
Open a GitHub release in the browser.
List contributors with git shortlog.
Write a manual release announcement post for the blog.
Run gh release create for v1.0.
Lint commit messages so they follow conventional commits going forward.
Tag the current commit as v1.2.0.
Show the diff between two tags.
